newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS-IHC Caland 1996 profit up 23.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-IHC Caland 1996 profit up 23.7 pct.

text.p: Dutch shipbuilding and engineering group IHC Caland NV on Monday reported final 1996 net profit up 23.7 percent as offshore activities blossomed.

The company said its healthy order book, which rose to 3.04 billion guilders ($1.6 billion) at the end of 1996 from 2.94 billion at the end of 1995, allowed it to repeat its forecast of 18 percent profit growth this year.

"Based on the current order portfolio and viable projects in the promising markets in which the group operates, management expects 1997 group net profit will rise by about 18 percent to some 110 million guilders," IHC Caland said in a statement.
But earnings per share (EPS) would rise by only 12 percent because of the issue of new shares last June, the company said.
Net profit for 1996 rose to 93.2 million guilders from 75.3 million in 1995. IHC Caland set a dividend of 1.80 guilders for 1996 versus 1.60 guilders the previous year.
The figures offered few surprises as the company in January said it expected 1996 profit of about 93 million guilders and an 18 percent profits rise in the current year.
At the close of the Amsterdam Stock Exchange, its shares stood down 0.80 guilders at 99.80.

Chairman Jan Bax said its offshore operations, mainly the construction of floating oil platforms, had contributed 70 percent of the profits. The remaining 30 percent was from shipbuilding, principally dredgers.
However, the company said profits on the shipbuilding side had suffered a bit from a "considerable loss" on one order for the construction of two large dredgers.
The big order caused problems and eventual delay in completion of one of the dredgers, which was destined for the Suez Canal. It was finally delivered last month.

Bax said he was not prepared to reveal the size of the loss on the order and, although he saw it as a one-off problem, he saw no way of definitely preventing a recurrence in future. "It's just part of the game," he said.
IHC Caland was more upbeat on its offshore operations which gained from a higher oil price boosting exploration activity.
Bax added that he was not worried even if oil prices dipped. "Consumption is growing, especially in the transport sector in the Far East and South America. The offshore side will stay good," he said.
Analysts said the headline figures were as expected, but the loss in dredger construction was not.

"The figures were in line, although the surprise was the sudden loss on the building of dredgers. It's a bad sign that they lost money, but their track record is such that we can probably assume it was a one-off," said Manus Fleskens of BZW.
He added that he remained positive on the company, but noted that an EPS rise of 12 percent, as forecast for 1997, would be lower than in previous years. ($ = 1.897 Dutch Guilders)
